debt_events.summary: Completed $3.97 billion refinancing: $2 billion 8.875% first-lien notes due 2031, $850 million first-lien term loan due 2031 and $1.12 billion 11.25% second-lien term loan due 2033. Term loans were issued at 1.5% and 1% original-issue discounts, respectively. Proceeds plus cash refinanced existing group debt; this is refinancing, not $3.97 billion of incremental liquidity.

Tender settled for $355.515 million of 7.5% notes due 2029; remaining notes were defeased for redemption around February 15, 2027. Redeemed subsidiary Muvico’s $903.4 million notes at par plus $144.3 million make-whole premium and accrued interest; repaid the existing AMC and Odeon term loans. Approximately 97% of debt maturities extended to 2031/2033, according to management.
Management stated it believed AMC was in full compliance with all agreements, including financial covenants, at quarter-end. This does not establish covenant compliance at November 3.
Form 10-Q Item 3, Defaults Upon Senior Securities: None. This is a quarter-specific disclosure, not evidence that no later default or distressed exchange occurred.

credit_ratings.summary: S&P: issuer credit rating B-, outlook Stable, unchanged in this release. New first-lien term loan and notes rated B+; new second-lien term loan rated CCC. Issue ratings and recovery differ materially from the issuer rating.
S&P upgraded issuer rating to B- from CCC+ and changed outlook to Stable from Negative; verified change within the preceding 12 months.

Moody’s, as reported by Investing.com: corporate family rating upgraded to B3 from Caa2; outlook Positive from Stable; speculative-grade liquidity rating SGL-3 from SGL-4. This is a secondary report, not an opened Moody’s release.

Fitch, according to a FrankNez article published September 12 and subsequently updated: first-time long-term issuer default rating B-, outlook Positive. Lower-confidence secondary-source evidence; the primary Fitch page did not expose its release text.

output.risk_rationale: As of 2026-11-03, credit and unsecured-counterparty risk is elevated: the latest filed quarter reports $3.9142 billion corporate debt principal and management warns that historical cash burn is unsustainable, although cash was $778.4 million ([Q2 10-Q](https://investor.amctheatres.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001411579-26-000059/amc-20260630x10q.htm)). The October 5 refinancing extended approximately 97% of debt to 2031/2033, materially reducing near-term refinancing pressure, while S&P maintained B-/Stable and Moody’s upgraded to B3/Positive ([refinancing](https://investor.amctheatres.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/443/amc-entertainment-holdings-inc-announces-results-of-tender-offer-the-closing-of-first-lien-notes-offering-and-new-term-loan-facilities-totaling-a-3-97-billion-refinancing-of-existing-debt); [S&P](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/3630718); [Moody’s report](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/moodys-upgrades-amc-rating-to-b3-on-debt-refinancing-plan-93CH-4909529)). Near-term payment capacity has improved, but substantial secured debt and speculative-grade ratings warrant conservative unsecured exposure and short settlement terms; the filing’s absence of senior-security defaults is not proof of timely supplier payment.

distress_signals.summary: Management said cash plus operating cash flow should cover obligations through the next 12 months, but historical cash burn was unsustainable long-term and additional liquidity beyond 12 months could not be assured. This is management liquidity-risk language, not an auditor going-concern opinion.

S&P expected a modest free-cash-flow deficit in 2026 and positive reported free cash flow in 2027; cited over $450 million annual interest and $850 million rent. These estimates precede the October refinancing and should not be treated as updated post-refinancing interest guidance.
Company scheduled third-quarter results for November 4, 2026, after this assessment cutoff; June 30 is therefore the latest quarterly financial period used here.

payment_behaviour.summary: Accounts payable were $396.7 million. The balance does not identify overdue amounts or establish payment speed; no supplier payment-performance conclusion can be drawn from it.
